steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Muslims believe Allah sent prophets (rasul and nabi) to every nation to guide people to the truth. All prophets brought the same message: worship one God and live righteously. Muhammad is the final and greatest prophet — the "Seal of the Prophets" (Surah 33:40).

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Risalah: Prophethood
steps.body: 1. For Risalah: Prophethood questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Risalah: Prophethood to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: The stories of the prophets are central to Muslim religious education in Britain. Madrasahs (Islamic schools) teach children about the lives and teachings of all the major prophets, emphasising their patience, courage and devotion to Allah.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: The Prophet’s migration from Makkah to Madinah (the Hijrah, 622 CE) marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. This event, commemorated every year by Muslims worldwide, symbolises the move from persecution to the establishment of a just community — a theme that resonates with British Muslims who value religious freedom and social justice.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two Muslim beliefs about prophethood. | "Muhammad is the most important prophet." Evaluate this statement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
